_what: The mAP yolo11n scores on the pinned COCO val2017 500-image subset, and every input that determines it. Read tests/integration/test_map_regression.py for how it is measured and src/yowo/benchmark/_baseline.py for how it is enforced.
_band: Two-sided. Repeat runs on one machine are bit-identical (0.41577614647708055, twice, 2026-09-15), so for a fixed model, fixed weights and a fixed image set the number should not move at all. The tolerance absorbs cross-machine float drift and nothing else. A rise past it means something changed that nobody declared.
_provenance: Measured locally first; measured_on records where. Confirmed 2026-09-15 on ubuntu x86-64 (CI run 34973410540): the band held, so cross-machine drift is inside +/-0.005 by measurement rather than assumption. If a CI number ever differs by more than the tolerance, the CI number becomes the baseline for a gate that runs on CI — the band is not widened to accommodate it, and load_baseline refuses a tolerance above 0.01 so it cannot be.
_shipped_default_cost: CONTEXT, NOT ENFORCED. The engine's default confidence_threshold is 0.25, not the COCO protocol's 0.001 this baseline uses. Measured once, 2026-09-15, over the same 500 images: 0.3658, 5.0 points lower. Recorded so the gap between the published-comparable number and what a user gets out of the box is visible rather than discovered. Nothing re-measures it, so treat it as dated.
_rerecord: All three of map_50_95, map_50 and map_75 are enforced against the band. To re-record deliberately: run `pytest tests/integration/test_map_regression.py -s`, which prints all three measured values, and update them together with measured_on and measured_at. A partial re-record fails the gate rather than leaving numbers that were never measured together. The gate never writes this file; only a human in a reviewed commit does.
